diagnostic_evidence.quote: The following \autoref{thm:equilibria} and \autoref{thm:expconv} follow from the logarithmic Sobolev inequality induced by displacement convexity, which is rigorously proved in~\cite{malrieu2001logarithmic} for the Euclidean space $\R^d$ and is carried over the torus with periodic boundary conditions.
We consider the case where the state space is the unit torus, $\Omega = \T^d = (\R/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^d$.

issues.failure_explanation: On $\T^d=(\R/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^d$, periodicity forces $\int_{\T^d}\Delta V\,dx=0$ for every $V\in C^2$, so $\nabla^2V\succeq\alpha I$ with $\alpha>0$ is unsatisfiable (it would imply $0\ge d\alpha|\T^d|>0$); likewise $\nabla^2W\succeq0$ on $\T^d$ forces $W$ to be constant. The convexity hypothesis is therefore vacuous in the paper's own setting, the advertised LSI yields no exponential convergence on the torus, and the asserted carry-over of the Euclidean displacement-convexity/LSI (malrieu2001logarithmic) to the torus is stated without any argument.

failure_location.quote: Namely, if $\nabla^2V(x)\succeq \alpha I$, and $\nabla^2 W(x)\succeq 0$ on $\T^d$, the free energy $\mathcal{F}[\mu]$ is displacement-convex, and one obtains a logarithmic Sobolev inequality that yields

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or rewrite the claim using the torus-adapted H-stability hypothesis and cite or prove a torus-specific logarithmic Sobolev inequality; keep thm:equilibria/thm:expconv tied to the cited literature.
issues.overall_effect: The introduction's exponential-convergence-under-convexity motivation is empty on the torus, and the heuristic support for thm:expconv (Euclidean LSI 'carried over') is unsubstantiated; the main text's H-stability hypothesis and all control results are unaffected.
issues.title: Convexity-based exponential convergence is vacuous on the torus
issues.why_classification: Motivational-level defect: the repair is a local rewrite, no advertised guarantee of the control theory is lost, and the main text already uses the correct torus-adapted hypothesis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under the above assumptions on $V,W,\sigma$ and any $\mu_0\in L^1_+(\Omega)$, there exists a unique variational solution $\mu(t)$ of \eqref{eq:mckean_vlasov_repeat}.

issues.failure_explanation: Two quantifier/hypothesis defects: (i) the theorem quantifies over any $\mu_0\in L^1_+(\Omega)$ without the standing normalization $\|\mu_0\|_{L^1}=1$ (stated only in the model paragraph), under which mass conservation fails; (ii) the claim $\mu(t,x)>0$ for all $x$ at all $t\ge0$ fails at $t=0$ for any datum vanishing on a set (e.g. $\mu_0=(2\pi)^{-d}\mathbf{1}_E$), and variational solutions are only defined a.e.; the valid statement is positivity for $t>0$ (a.e.).

failure_location.quote: {\bf Mass and positivity:} for all times $t \ge 0$, $\int_{\Omega} \mu(t,x) \, dx =1$ and $\mu(t,x)>0$ for all $x \in \Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add $\|\mu_0\|_{L^1}=1$ to the theorem's hypotheses and replace 'for all times $t\ge0$, $\mu(t,x)>0$ for all $x$' by positivity for $t>0$ almost everywhere.
issues.overall_effect: The mass/positivity clause of thm:wellposed is false as stated at $t=0$ and for non-normalized data; existence, uniqueness, and energy dissipation are unaffected.
issues.title: thm:wellposed: positivity asserted at t=0 for arbitrary L^1_+ data; mass hypothesis omitted
issues.why_classification: A boundary-case quantifier fix restores the statement with the standard strong-maximum-principle content; no method, rate, or advertised scope is lost.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the proposition by deleting 'real' (keeping compact resolvent and discreteness), and re-justify stabilizability and the Riccati theory for the non-self-adjoint $\Lcal_0$ (e.g. prove a Riesz basis of root vectors for $\Lcal_0$, or use a Hautus-sufficient infinite-dimensional LQ result valid without self-adjointness).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised self-adjoint Schrödinger spectral structure (real eigenvalues, orthogonal spectral picture) is withdrawn; compact resolvent, discreteness, finiteness of unstable modes (lem:spectrum_finite), and the Hautus verification itself survive. Because the stabilizability/Riccati steps (thm:hautus via Curtain-Zwart Thm 5.2.11, prop:ARE, and transitively thm:nonlin-existence and thm:local-decay) are cast in a spectral framework whose self-adjointness/Riesz-spectrality is not established and is false as used, those conclusions are unreliable until re-justified for the non-self-adjoint operator.
